title: Evaluate ML Models and Foundation Models Against Requirements
objective: Compare traditional ML, foundation models, RAG, and customization options based on quality, explainability, latency, cost, and security.

prerequisites.title: Prepare Data for ML and AI

sections.title: Choose an approach based on the problem to solve and its constraints
paragraphs: ML engineers do not choose a foundation model simply because the requirement says to “use AI.” They examine the expected output—such as prediction, classification, summarization, search, or generation—as well as whether labeled data is available, explainability, latency, cost, and data confidentiality. They then compare traditional ML, managed services, pretrained models, and foundation models.

Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed service that provides secure access to foundation models from leading AI companies. Rather than judging performance by the model name alone, evaluate each option against operational requirements, including the target task, input constraints, output quality, Region and usage conditions, and guardrails.

sources.label: MLA-C02 Exam Guide: Selecting a Modeling Approach

sections.title: Managing Training and Customization for Comparability
paragraphs: For model training and fine-tuning, record the data version, code, hyperparameters, execution environment, and output artifacts. If the conditions for each experiment cannot be tracked, it is impossible to determine whether performance differences are caused by the data, configuration, random seeds, or implementation.

Fine-tuning, continual pre-training, prompt design, and RAG are not alternatives to one another. If organization-specific knowledge is updated frequently, consider RAG; if behavior or format must be changed consistently, consider customization. Choose based on evaluation and safety requirements.

sources.label: MLA-C02 Exam Guide: Training and Customization

sections.title: Evaluate Based on Use Cases and Failure Examples
paragraphs: Evaluators do not adopt a model based solely on a single accuracy metric. They define the cost of business errors, quality for each data slice, latency, throughput, safety, and reproducibility, and measure them using evaluation data that was not used for training. For generative AI, they add use-case-appropriate criteria such as factuality, instruction following, faithfulness to sources, and harmful outputs.

Evaluation results are stored together with the inputs, expected results, model version, prompt or settings, and measurements. They classify failure examples and select improvement candidates. If the model does not meet the thresholds, they do not deploy it and decide whether to review the data, approach, prompt, or model.

sources.label: MLA-C02 Exam Guide: Analyzing and Evaluating Performance

checkpoints.prompt: The person responsible for a feature that summarizes customer inquiries wants it to reference the company's internal policies in their most up-to-date form. Which approach is most appropriate to consider first?

choices.text: Retrain the entire foundation model every time to reflect policy updates.
choices.explanation: This is excessive for the update requirement and does not directly resolve source verification.

choices.text: Evaluate the policies' update frequency, search accuracy, source attribution, and access controls, and consider RAG as needed.
choices.explanation: This meets the requirement to reference frequently changing knowledge with supporting sources.

choices.text: Have the model answer using only its general knowledge without referring to the policies.
choices.explanation: This cannot guarantee that the company's latest internal policies are reflected.

checkpoints.prompt: The person responsible for a fraud detection model wants to investigate later why two training experiments produced different performance results. Which record is most appropriate?

choices.text: Keep only the highest evaluation score and delete the experimental conditions.
choices.explanation: The results cannot be compared or reproduced.

choices.text: For each experiment, save the data version, code, hyperparameters, execution environment, random-seed settings, and output artifacts.
choices.explanation: The cause of the performance difference can be compared under reproducible conditions.

choices.text: Overwrite the evaluation data so that the results always appear to be the same.
choices.explanation: This undermines the reliability of the evaluation.

checkpoints.prompt: Before putting a generative AI response-support feature into production, evaluators will decide whether to adopt it. Which is the most appropriate basis for this decision?

choices.text: Use the fact that it responded successfully once in a demo as the sole basis for adoption.
choices.explanation: This does not allow reproducibility or behavior in failure scenarios to be evaluated.

choices.text: Adopt the first candidate that works without setting evaluation thresholds.
choices.explanation: This does not allow adoption decisions to be made consistently.

choices.text: Measure use-case-specific quality, results by data slice, latency, cost, safety, and faithfulness to supporting evidence using independent evaluation data.
choices.explanation: This enables candidates to be compared while taking business requirements and risks into account.
